evidence.correctness: node scratchpad/writer/check.mjs ventures/freelance-writer-rate-calculator/calc.mjs (script in the run's scratchpad; inputs listed in checks). Worked example recomputed by hand: 1500/500 + 4 + 2x1 = 9 h, 300/9 = 33.33, 500/9 = 55.56, 75 x 9 = 675, 675/1500 = 0.45: all match. The contradictory finding from 2026-11-13 is gone ($0.50/word vs $400 now shows only 'per-word pays $38.89/hr more'). Still wrong: blank writing speed with 1,500 words gives 6 h, $50/h and '100% of the total time is research and revisions' with no warning; the solver's $0.0125/word prints as '$0.01/word' (money() still rounds to cents, 20% low). money(0.1) now prints '$0.10' and is locale-fixed (en-US).
evidence.completeness: Same feature list as 2026-11-13 runs end to end in node (comparison, solver, floor flag, ghostwriting note, tie, clamping); 42 tests. README 'Known gaps' honestly lists four open items. Served page not loaded (marisstella.app returns proxy 403 from this session).
evidence.verification: cd ventures/freelance-writer-rate-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 42 pass, 0 fail. Four mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: the two that survived on 2026-11-13 still survive (0.25 threshold >= -> >; tie tolerance 0.005 -> 0.5); the new per-word guard (betterOption !== 'per-word' -> true) and blank-speed fallback are caught. One test was added by PR #15342 (41 -> 42).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (194 lines) and index.html script (lines 175-273). money() now pins en-US and pads one-decimal output; still one formatter for dollars and per-word rates. Silent fallbacks unchanged: num() turns blank/zero speed into 0 writing hours; page does Number(v)||0. Low-rate title says 'at or below' while the test is strict <.
evidence.claims: Unchanged from 2026-11-13: index.html:56 promises 'which one actually pays more, not just which headline number looks bigger', but the verdict equals the bigger total in 144 of 144 grid cases (check.mjs). The FAQ (index.html:14 JSON-LD and :150) still says heavy research makes a flat fee 'usually pay a higher effective hourly rate than an equivalent per-word rate', which hours cannot cause. calc.mjs:26 'multiple 2026 rate-guide sources agree' and :59 'every 2026 rate guide above agrees' unchanged. Disclaimer, privacy and DNT/GPC opt-out present and tested.
evidence.fitness: Same job as 2026-11-13 ($0.20/word or $500 for 1,500 researched words): the solver ($675 for $75/h) is the useful output; the verdict repeats the totals. Self-employment tax, overrun and extra-round risk not modelled.
evidence.domain: Compared against IRS Schedule SE (15.3% on 92.35% of net earnings) and Peak Freelance / bestwriting.com 2026 rate guides as in the prior audit. Effective-hourly-over-all-hours method is standard; the 'per-word does not pay research' framing is wrong economics for a given offer; gross hourly with no SE adjustment ($55.56 gross is $47.71 after SE tax).

Blank or zero writing speed with a nonzero word count silently drops writing time and still shows hourly rates and a verdict.

Hourly is gross of US self-employment tax (about 14.1% of net); overrun, extra-round and kill-fee risk not modelled.
Source wording overstates agreement: 'every 2026 rate guide agrees' on $0.05-$0.10 entry; 16-20% ghostwriting premium from 'multiple' sources is one 213-writer survey.
Solved per-word rates are rounded to cents: $0.0125/word prints as '$0.01/word'.
